purpose: Record the already observed signatures of the pinned Mathlib APIs used by the two pending Fubini modules; diagnostic background only.

upstream.retrieval: Official GitHub file contents fetched at this exact commit. Code search was used only to locate files; all signature conclusions below use the pinned file contents.

checks.observed_signature: For alpha : Fin (n + 1) -> Type, the equivalence maps (forall j, alpha j) to alpha i x (forall j, alpha (i.succAbove j)).
checks.conclusion: The constant real-valued family and pivot zero used by split4 and split3 match this domain and codomain.

checks.observed_signature: MeasurePreserving.symm has an explicit measurable equivalence argument and a measure-preservation proof; the pinned Integral/Pi.lean itself uses (measurePreserving_piFinSuccAbove ...).symm.integral_comp'.
checks.conclusion: The explicit equivalence parameter does not establish a missing-argument error in the project's matching dot-notation call.

checks.observed_signature: For h : MeasurePreserving f mu nu and g on the codomain, the conclusion equates the integral of g (f x) against mu with the integral of g against nu.
checks.conclusion: Applying this to the inverse measurable equivalence and taking the symmetry of the resulting equality has the direction used by the project.

checks.observed_signature: The explicit arguments are the product-space function f followed by hf : Integrable f (mu.prod nu). The conclusion integrates the first coordinate outside the second coordinate.
checks.conclusion: The project's integral_prod f hf calls and coordinate order match the pinned signature.

checks.observed_signature: For a product-integrable f, the conclusion is: for mu-almost every x, the function y -> f (x, y) is integrable against nu.
checks.conclusion: The slices used by integral_fin_three and integral_fin_four have the correct outer and inner coordinate order.

checks.observed_signature: The theorem takes f and g as explicit arguments and equates the integral of f z.1 * g z.2 with the product of their integrals; it has no additional explicit Integrable premises.
checks.conclusion: The two-coordinate separation calls integral_prod_mul _ _ do not omit an explicit integrability argument.

checks.observed_signature: The pinned library contains insertNth_zero and zero_succAbove, uses the same insertNthEquiv conversion in Integral/Pi.lean, and defines Matrix.vecCons h t as Fin.cons h t.
checks.conclusion: The coordinate conversions and vector concatenations have the required declaration and definitional-equality basis. Closure of the project's concrete simp goals has not been compiled.

checks.observed_signature: piFinTwoEquiv has inverse p -> Fin.cons p.1 (Fin.cons p.2 finZeroElim); MeasurableEquiv.piFinTwo uses that equivalence.
checks.conclusion: The two-coordinate inverse in split2_symm has the expected underlying definition for its coordinatewise reduction.

checks.observed_signature: integral_congr uses EqOn over uIcc. integral_of_le converts the oriented interval integral to a set integral over Ioc. integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo equates that set integral with the Ioo integral under the declared atomless-measure assumptions.
checks.conclusion: The project's uIcc_of_le step and Ioc-to-Ioo rewrites match these signatures and directions.

checks.observed_signature: The theorem consumes compactness and continuity on the set. The pinned library's compact-interval adapter itself calls hf.integrableOn_compact isCompact_Icc.
checks.conclusion: The project's parameter order and dot-notation calls match the pinned API; actual instance synthesis remains a compilation obligation.

findings.meaning: No definite API mismatch was found in the listed checks. This is not evidence that either complete Lean file elaborates or passes its proof obligations.
